findings.summary: The port keeps a CJK literal in the engine and the new test suite asserts it, violating PRD Requirement 6 ('English ... No CJK characters remain in engine or tests') and the acceptance check 'a CJK scan over engine and tests find nothing'. `ACCEPTANCE_HEADINGS` contains "## 验收标准" (orch.py:40) and test_orch.py:623 writes a prd_body containing that same CJK heading; the code comment calls it 'an allowed, documented i18n exception', but the PRD grants no such exception.
findings.failure_scenario:
Run the acceptance check `grep -rnP '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]'` (or any CJK scan) over packages/cli/src/templates/trellis/orchestrator and test/python/orchestrator: it matches orch.py:40 (`"## 验收标准"`) and test_orch.py:623 (`prd_body="# x

## 验收标准
- ok
"`). The AC item 'a CJK scan over engine and tests find nothing (generic wording only)' therefore fails, and the shipped engine still carries non-English text. (Verified: a Python CJK-range scan over both trees returns exactly these two lines and nothing else.)
findings.evidence:
engine scan -> `orch.py:40: ACCEPTANCE_HEADINGS = ("## Acceptance Criteria", "## 验收标准")`; test scan -> `tests/test_orch.py:623: self._planned([child_spec("api")], prd_body="# x

## 验收标准
- ok
")`. Both are part of the port delta (spark had no such acceptance-heading alias in this form).

findings.summary: PRD Requirement 4's reviewer card rename (`check` -> `review-finder`) has no test: no assertion anywhere pins the agent a reviewer/finder is dispatched with. Reverting the name back to the old `check` (or a typo) keeps the entire unittest suite green, so the requirement is not actually covered. (The verifier rename `check-verify` -> `review-verify` IS pinned by RespawnAgentTest at line 1819, and implement/simplify are pinned too, which makes the finder gap stand out.)
findings.failure_scenario: Mutate the engine — replace every `"review-finder"` with `"check"` in pipeline.py and integration.py (AGENT_BY_KIND['review'], _start_finder, _start_single_finder, _start_integration_review) — then run `python3 -m unittest test_pipeline test_orch test_guard`: 290 tests, still OK (no failure). So a regression that reverts reviewers to a card that is no longer installed would pass `pnpm test` while at runtime every review round's finder worker fails to start, stalling the orchestration at `reviewing`.
findings.evidence: Only agent-pinning assertions found: test_pipeline.py:1103 (`agent == 'implement'`), 1807 (`'simplify'`), 1819 (`'review-verify'`). Grep of all test files for `review-finder` yields only test_orch.py:643 (the REQUIRED_TRACKED_PATHS string), never a spawn-agent assertion. The mutation experiment above confirms the suite stays green with `review-finder`->`check`.

findings.summary: `DefaultMainRootTests.test_main_root_is_repo_root` was weakened during the port: it now compares `inject.MAIN_ROOT` against `Path(inject.__file__).resolve().parents[2]`, which is literally the expression inject.py uses to define MAIN_ROOT, so the assertion is a tautology that can never fail. In spark it compared against the actual repo root (the tests dir's parents[3]).
findings.failure_scenario: If `inject.MAIN_ROOT` were broken (wrong parents index / different resolution), this test still passes because both sides are derived from the same expression; a regression in inject's default MAIN_ROOT resolution is therefore undetected. Only the sibling `test_hook_runs_without_orch_main_root` gives (partial) cover.
findings.evidence: new: `repo_root = Path(inject.__file__).resolve().parents[2]; self.assertEqual(inject.MAIN_ROOT, repo_root)`; old (spark): `repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]; self.assertEqual(inject.MAIN_ROOT, repo_root)` — the old form tied MAIN_ROOT to a location independent of the module's own definition.
